scope: HostRenderer and the canonical native Engine present a CPU frame through winit/softbuffer and a Vello GPU frame into a host-owned wgpu TextureView on a real X11 protocol surface supplied by Xvfb.

one_frame_clean_exit.observed: HostRenderer bound the active Surface generation, winit created the X11 window, softbuffer acquired its surface and presented one Blitz/Vello CPU frame; the translated event stream contained ImeEnabled(false) and pointer Hover.

gpu_one_frame_clean_exit.observed: The host owned the X11 Surface and wgpu device; HostRenderer rendered through Vello hybrid directly into the acquired Surface texture, the host queue presented it and gpu_presented acknowledged the exact live generation.

resize_capture.observed: The X11 configure/resize path repainted the complete 640x360 surface; both fixed 200x120 rectangles remained at 24000 pixels each.

limitations: Xvfb provides a real X11 protocol surface but not a compositor, window manager, hardware display controller or vsync.
The resize capture validates repaint and surface reconfiguration, not suspend/resume delivery by a platform session manager.
The capture script terminates the long-running diagnostic after taking both screenshots; the separate --once run validates clean application exit after present.
The GPU window uses the llvmpipe software Vulkan adapter; no hardware GPU swapchain, device-loss recovery, real system accessibility bridge or live external IME service is claimed.
The scene/update orchestration proof remains separate; this report is presentation integration evidence.
diagnostics: Early recapture attempts used a fixed four-second startup delay and timed out during VM recompilation before the winit window existed. The runner now waits up to 300 seconds for the exact window title while checking that the process remains alive; the successful run above used that path.
